newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian SGB to hold div steady post-Tractebel buy.
newsitem.headline: Belgian SGB to hold div steady post-Tractebel buy.

text.p: Societe Generale de Belgique, Belgium's flagship holding company, said on Tuesday 1996 dividend would not fall because of its 49 billion franc purchase of 24.7 percent of Tractebel.
Chairman Etienne Davignon told a news conference on first half earnings, "The purchase of Tractebel will have no influence on our capacity to maintain the dividend policy we have been following."
He said this meant there would be no decrease in the 1996 dividend.
Davignon had no comment on whether there would be an increase in this year's dividend.

SGB has taken on 72 billion francs of syndicated bank debt to finance its Tractebel purchase. Davignon noted the extra dividend income from its Tractebel stake would be greater than the cost of servicing the extra debt.
Part of the new debt is a 48 billion credit line agreed last week with six banks -- Generale Bank, Deutsche Bank, Banque Indosuez, Banque Nationale de Paris, Kredietbank and ASLK/CGER.
Davignon said SGB already had available to it a 24 billion franc credit line agreed in July and around eight billion francs of cash in hand.

The difference between the purchase price of the Tractebel stake and the 80 billion francs in credit lines and cash was to cover any demand from SGB's 14,500 franc per share public offer for the rest of Tractebel's issued capital on October 9-30.

Davignon reiterated SGB was not aiming to obtain 100 percent of Tractebel. The offer was made to small shareholders to give them the same conditions as holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert SA (GBL), the seller of the Tractebel shares.

In an effort to dissuade shareholders from taking SGB up on its offer for the stock, SGB is offering them a put warrant. The warrant, guaranteeing the shareholders a 14,500 franc price in three years' time, gives the stock added value.
"If we had thought that Tractebel would not be worth 14,500 francs in three years, we would not have bought it," Davignon said, commenting on the public offer.
Davignon said U.S. authorities had cleared the Tractebel buy, which was completed on Monday.
